statement: Ella rolls a red die and a blue die. Each die shows a number from 1 to 6. In how many different ways can the two numbers add up to 9?

choices.misconception: I counted 3 and 6 and then 4 and 5, and forgot that the red and blue dice can swap their numbers.
I thought every number on the red die has a partner on the blue die, so I counted 6 ways.
I also counted 1 and 8, 2 and 7, 7 and 2, and 8 and 1, but a die only goes up to 6.
I thought there must be 9 ways because the total is 9.

hints: Start with the red die showing 1. Can the blue die show what you need?
Go through the red die’s numbers in order and find what the blue die must show each time. Cross out any case needing more than 6. Red 3 with blue 6 differs from red 6 with blue 3.
Red 1 needs blue 8 and red 2 needs blue 7, which a die cannot show. Red 3 needs blue 6, which works. Keep going up to red 6.

solutions.reliable: Red 1 would need blue 8 and red 2 would need blue 7, but a die only goes up to 6, so those do not work. Red 3 and blue 6, red 4 and blue 5, red 5 and blue 4, red 6 and blue 3 all work. That makes 4 ways. The idea to keep: fix one thing at a time and list in order, then check every case against the rules, here that a die shows only 1 to 6.
solutions.elegant: The biggest a die can show is 6, so each die must show at least 9 - 6 = 3. The red die can be 3, 4, 5 or 6, and each choice fixes the blue die, so there are 4 ways.

whyOnTest: Listing ways to make a total checks systematic listing: go in order, treat the two dice as different, and drop the cases a die cannot show.
author: Devansh Sanghavi
